pageCache.pageTitle: Reach Academy Feltham - Providing students with the skills, attributes, and academic qualifications to enjoy lives of choice and opportunity.
pageCache.text:
Our mission is to equip all of our pupils with the skills, attributes and academic qualifications to enable them to go on to enjoy lives of choice and opportunity.
Our vision
Every single child will gain the skills, attributes and academic qualifications to enjoy a life of choice and opportunity.
celebrating our Ofsted results
For Educators
Join our fantastic Reach Out community: a place where passionate educators can share, collaborate and grow.
You’ll be given access to exclusive content, blogs, updates on events, and our latest vacancies. We look forward to seeing you soon!
Reach Academy Feltham wins Global Award for Teacher Development
We were also shortlisted in the top 10 schools for the Global Schools Award 2026.
Welcome from our Co-headteachers
Welcome to Reach Academy Feltham!Our staff are all driven by our mission to equip all of our pupils with the skills, attitudes and academic qualifications to enable them to go on to enjoy lives of choice and opportunity. Our school focuses on bringing together the whole community in a shared dedication to do whatever it takes to achieve successful outcomes for the children we all love and care for…
Who are we?
Reach Academy Feltham is a highly successful and nurturing all-through school for 4-18 year olds. It was founded by a group of teachers who know that all children can achieve great things.
Our unique and effective structure promotes a sense of community and continuity that has resulted in significant success over the past decade. We are dedicated to training excellent teachers, building strong community relationships, and realising the potential of every pupil.
Delivering excellent teaching, achieving great results.
What makes our model successful?
All-through
From nursery to sixth-form. This structure enables pupils to feel part of our school, all the way through their school career. It also means we’re able to walk with families through many important milestones.
Excellent teaching
Reach Academy Feltham is filled with committed teachers doing their utmost to ensure that pupils realise their potential. Our educators are committed to thoughtful and effective professional development.
Small school
Having only 60 pupils max in each year group ensures strong personal relationships and high levels of personalisation. We can create a community where no pupil is left behind.
Clear expectations
We expect all pupils to work hard and be respectful of others at all times. During the school day we work to minimise distractions and maximise joy and learning.
High aspirations
Every pupil will work towards top grades and the opportunity to succeed at a top university. Our aim is for every student to flourish on their chosen career path.
Studying at Reach Academy Feltham
Not only do we offer an all-through education from Reception to Year 11, we also welcome toddlers to our exciting nursery and young adults to our innovative college. Find out about learning at Reach Academy Feltham and why our methods are so effective.
Teaching careers at Reach Academy Feltham
You will have noticed that we love to talk about excellent teaching. This is because Reach Academy Feltham has an incredibly passionate, skilled, and supportive team. We are committed to effective professional development and also offer a variety of ways to begin a career in teaching through our exciting teacher training courses.
Train to Teach at Reach
If you want to get into teaching, look no further. We offer excellent teacher training in west London. Whether you’re looking for a PGCE or QTS qualification, we support you all the way.
You will be taught by experts who are still teaching at our fantastic schools here in Feltham, and your in school practise will be either here or in the surrounding areas.

pageCache.pageTitle: Ethos and values - Reach Academy Feltham
pageCache.text:
Our ethos and values
Discover our drive to pursue excellent work and explore the ‘Reach’ values
Reach Academy Feltham is a small school. We place meaningful relationships at the heart of everything we do. We designed the school building, arranged the timetable and focus staff time on nurturing these strong relationships. Leaders and teachers ensure all of the children experience consistency and continuity through their school career; knowing more, doing more and developing socially and emotionally over time. The school staff work closely with families and experts to ensure that all children are able to thrive and lead healthy and happy lives both now and in the future. This includes not allowing mobile phones in school, ensuring healthy eating and regular exercise is promoted and enabled, and working with families to create healthy age-appropriate routines around things such as a sleep.
Our core values
Why ‘Reach’ ?
‘Reflect’ embodies a core value at Reach Academy Feltham because we believe in the power of constant learning from ourselves and others. It’s about taking a moment to think before we act, learning from our mistakes, and understanding ourselves at a deeper level. This reflective practice cultivates self-awareness and fosters personal growth.
Endeavouring or working hard is another value we uphold. At Reach Schools, we subscribe to the idea that success is the product of hard work, not luck. We pour 100% of our effort into everything we do, whether it’s tackling academic challenges or finding solutions to problems. We embrace the ethos that our dedication and industriousness are the keys to achievement.
Aspiration is a driving force at Reach Schools. We dare to dream, and we instill the bravery in our students to make those dreams a reality. This involves cultivating self-belief and, at times, leading others towards a shared vision. When we aspire, we encourage ourselves to plan for greatness, believe in our abilities, and guide others on the journey.
Showing courage, perhaps one of the most challenging values to live by, is integral to our school’s ethos. Whether it’s revealing our weaknesses or strengths, we encourage our students to embrace vulnerability and risk. We teach them to not fear making mistakes, to persist in the face of adversity, and to think creatively. This courage forms the bedrock of resilience and innovation.
Finally, ‘Have Fun‘ is a value that encapsulates our belief in the joy of learning. When exploring the other values, having fun comes naturally. But sometimes, we also need to relax and have fun to get the most out of the other values. We foster an environment where students are passionate about what they do, show kindness to themselves and others, and work well in teams. This value reminds us that whilst education is about academic success, it’s also about enjoying the journey and supporting each other along the way.

About Reach Academy Feltham
A brief summary of our vision, model and environment
Our vision
That every single pupil will leave us with the skills, attributes and academic qualifications to go on to enjoy lives of choice and opportunity.
Our intended outcomes for our pupils aged 18 are that:
Our school
Reach Academy Feltham (RAF) is an all-through, mixed, non-selective, and non-denominational school serving pupils from ages 2 to 18. The school first opened its doors in September 2012, welcoming its inaugural cohort of Year 7 and Reception pupils. An expansion in Autumn 2015 saw the opening of a Nursery, allowing the school to accept pupils as young as two years old.
Our ‘all-through’ approach
Our ‘all-through’ structure is designed to create a sense of belonging and continuity for pupils. This approach allows pupils to remain within the same educational environment from an early age, right through to sixth form. It provides an opportunity to nurture pupils’ strengths and support them in overcoming any weaknesses from an early age. It also mitigates the typical challenges pupils face when transitioning from a smaller primary school to a larger secondary institution.
Our carefully designed environment
We believe that community and strong relationships matter. Our purpose-built design, with each floor of the building being home to ‘Phases’ containing three year groups, means our approach emulates the feel of a smaller school within a larger community, aiding in creating consistency and familiarity as students make the sometimes daunting transition from primary to secondary education. Pupils are able to remain in an environment where they know their teachers and peers, and are truly known by them.
The academy model
Academies are state-funded, independently governed schools designed to cater to local children. Reach Academy Feltham was established by a group of teachers who firmly believe in the potential for greatness in every child. A number of the founding staff members remain involved including Rebecca Cramer, the CEO, and Beck Owen, the former Co-Headteacher (Secondary). More than 50% of the staff body have been at the school for more than 5 years, providing stability for our families.
More about Reach Academy Feltham

Our partners
Find out about the organisations that help us to deliver excellent care to our students
The organisations we’re working with.
We are delighted to work with a range of organisations to deliver an excellent education that puts our pupils on a path to a life of choice and opportunity. Some of other key partnerships are:
Place 2 Be
We have partnered with Place2Be since the school opened in 2012 to ensure that our pupils can access professional counselling on site much more quickly than they could access it from other agencies. We have a model that means 35 of our pupils are able to access counselling at the same time, and the service also offers a drop-in for pupils and support for staff too.
Family Links
We work with Family Links to offer a range of nurturing programmes for our parents and wider community. More than 150 of our parents have taken a course delivered by our Family Support team.
Sport Impact
We work with Sport Impact to maximise the impact of the Primary Sport Premium. Sport Impact help to improve the quality of PE teaching throughout the school and ensure that our pupils have access to a range of competition opportunities.
The Reach Foundation
The Reach Foundation, provides an integrated pipeline of support for children, young people and families in Feltham to improve outcomes. Through shared expertise and services, we are able to serve our community.
Family Group
We work with The School & Family Works to run our Family Group for parents/carers and children where children are at risk of failing in school due to behavioural, emotional and/or family issues.

pageCache.pageTitle: RAF - Co-headteachers welcome - Reach Academy Feltham
pageCache.text:
Meet our co-headteachers
Meet Harpreet Dhillon and Manjit More
Letter from Harpreet and Manjit
Welcome to Reach Academy Feltham, part of Reach Schools. Our staff are all driven by our mission to equip all of our pupils with the skills, attitudes and academic qualifications to enable them to go on to enjoy lives of choice and opportunity. Our school focuses on bringing together the whole community in a shared dedication to do whatever it takes to achieve successful outcomes for the children we all love and care for. We have the highest academic expectations whilst maintaining a loving, family-focused culture. As the Co-headteachers, and supported by our Senior Leadership Team, we aim to know every pupil as an individual, harnessing the power of family relationships and all-through knowledge, to ensure that we can tailor our curriculum, support and resources to meet each child’s needs and desires. We believe that strong foundations in English and mathematics are crucial to life-long success and happiness of all children. We are committed to providing life-enhancing opportunities for all pupils, including access to a broad and balanced curriculum and extensive extra-curricular activities, trips and residential stays. The all-through nature of our school provides unique opportunities for students to have, and then become, role models and experience leadership opportunities. The strength of relationships with staff and peers enables all students to flourish. Pupils join us at the age of 4 (many having been to our Reach Up Nursery from the age of 2 years old) and progress seamlessly through transitions all the way to the age of 18 years old. This provides you, and your child(ren) with stability and a sense of ‘home from home’ that we believe school should provide to all. We use our small site to its full potential, including our roof-top pitch, 4-court sports hall and specialist science labs, music, drama, art and food technology suites. Our youngest students have separate play spaces to ensure they can explore in the safest environment possible and our older students have staggered break times so that they have ample space to play freely. We are ambitious. We believe your child(ren) deserves nothing less than the very best from us and, with your help, we know that we have a winning formula that will result in happy, healthy children who are able to thrive academically.
We are delighted to welcome you to our wonderful school.
More about Reach Academy Feltham

pageCache.pageTitle: Reach's Language Superstars - Reach Academy Feltham
pageCache.text:
Reach’s Language Superstars
At Reach Academy Feltham, three pupils have been highly commended by the Anthea Bell Prize for Young Translators. They submitted a total of nineteen translations in four different languages to the Prize and of those, four received commendations.
Commendations for Translation Skills
Danyal Kazmi (17) received two high commendations for Mandarin and Spanish, Alice Valcheva (12) was highly commended for Russian, while Rawan Adam (17) was highly commended for French.
More than 25 thousand young people took part in this national competition recognising creative translation. It is open to pupils aged 11-18 at schools across the UK and is run by the University of Oxford’s Queen’s College. The prize is named after Anthea Bell OBE (1936–2018) who is considered one of the leading literary translators of the 20th and 21st centuries.
Head of Languages at Reach Academy Feltham, Chloe Sides said:
“I am incredibly proud of all of our linguists who took part in the Anthea Bell Translation Prize and want to congratulate Danyal, Rawan and Alice who have been awarded a commendation in such a highly respected competition. What an achievement! At Reach, we truly value languages, ensuring that all of our pupils are able to sit a GCSE in at least one language (with many choosing to do two or even three). Our students know that the skills and knowledge developed through language study will lead to a life of choice and opportunity which is why we are so pleased to run A-level language study through the Languages For All programme.”
Youngest A* ever in Sanskrit?
Meanwhile, Lakshmi from Reach Academy Hanworth Park has been honoured by the Indian High Commission in London for receiving an A* in Sanskrit iGCSE aged just thirteen. Lakshmi has been learning the subject in her own time over the past three years and had to teach herself the script before learning to understand the language.
Lakshmi, her parents and Co-headteacher Louis Everett travelled to meet the High Commissioner and be congratulated. She has also received a Certificate of Appreciation by the High Commission of India in recognition of her outstanding achievements.
Lakshmi’s parents said:
‘We are incredibly proud of our daughter for receiving this wonderful recognition. To see our daughter connect so well with Sanskrit, and achieve this level of knowledge at such an early age is extraordinary.”
Co-headteacher Louis Everett said:
“What Lakshmi has achieved is extraordinary. Sanskrit is an incredibly complex and difficult language to learn. To achieve the very top grade is a phenomenal feat in itself but Lakshmi has achieved this whilst continuing to perform strongly in all her academic subjects and engaging in a range of creative arts and sporting enrichment.”

Primary Clubs
We are delighted to be able to offer you a wealth of extra-curricular options for your child(ren).
Extra-curricular clubs
We have a diverse range of extra-curricular options for our Primary pupils throughout the academic year and we encourage as many people to sign up to these great opportunities to extend their skills and learning.
Club Timings and Dates
All primary clubs run from 15.30 – 16.30.
Cycle 1 will be 13 weeks long, except Mondays which will be 12 weeks long.
This starts on Monday 14th September and finishes on Friday 18th December.
*FSM – Entitled to Free School Meals.
Drama (Superheroes save the Earth)
Tag Rugby Introduction
£32.50 for the cycle
Poetry (Starts on Wednesday 21st october)
Costs
The prices of clubs vary depending on the activity. All prices can be found above and are payable via the MCAS app.
Please note that there will not be any refunds for pupil illness or if a child cannot attend their club (including if they are on a trip or residential). Some clubs are free and may have sessions cancelled throughout the cycle due to staffing and spacing. If this occurs, then you will be notified as soon as possible.
Most clubs will take place outside, even if weather conditions are poor. If there is no choice but to cancel the club due to weather, you will not receive a refund.
How to sign up
Clubs are allocated on a first come, first served basis. If you would like to sign your child up for a club, you can do this on the MCAS app. If you sign your child up on this app, they will automatically have a place in this club.
Dismissal after clubs
Years Reception – Year 6 will be dismissed from the secondary playground promptly after their club. Please ensure your child is collected promptly or they will be placed in Kid Space on an emergency charge of £10.
Clothing for clubs
Full Reach PE kit is required for sports clubs and children will be dismissed in their PE kit.
Non-sports clubs will take place in school uniform.
Strike System
In Years 1-6 we operate a 2 strike system. If your child’s behaviour is disruptive or inappropriate within a club then they will receive a strike. The first strike is a warning, however if your child receives a second strike in a cycle then they will not be allowed to continue with that specific club during that cycle and no refunds will be offered.
Food Prior to Clubs
Students are welcome to bring a snack to eat before their club starts. Students are only allowed to bring fruit or vegetables to eat. If their snack is not a fruit or vegetable, they will not be able to eat it until after their club.

pageCache.pageTitle: RAF Our curriculum - Reach Academy Feltham
pageCache.text:
Our curriculum
Find out about our all-through, backwards-planned curriculum
Our intentional and carefully planned curriculum drives progress to excellent outcomes through establishing a powerful knowledge base and a life-long love of learning.
As an all-through school, Reach Academy Feltham has considered the knowledge, skills and attitudes that are required to achieve academic excellence in each subject at A Level and beyond. Subject leaders and teachers then plan backwards from this point. This ensures that pupils in each phase receive a rigorous, coherent and intelligently sequenced curriculum, which builds on what has come before. The curriculum at Reach is grounded in the strongest available evidence about how pupils learn and retain knowledge in the long term – focusing in particular on research from cognitive science.
More about Reach Academy Feltham
Curriculum Principles
Backwards planned and deliberately sequenced
Our curriculum is designed backwards from success at A Level and beyond. We think carefully about what children need to be able to do, know and say at each point to ensure success. This sequencing ensures that pupils spiral back to key concepts throughout their learning within a subject and that these key concepts get progressively more challenging over time.
Knowledge rich, embedding key knowledge deeply and durably
We ensure that we are constantly developing both substantive and disciplinary knowledge throughout subject areas. The knowledge that pupils need is clearly mapped and regular retrieval ensures that this is learnt and remembered overtime. Direct instruction and use of careful questioning, alongside periods of practice ensures the durability and flexibility of this knowledge. Our research driven approach to teaching and learning ensures that teachers have the strategies they need to create change in pupils long term memory.
Carefully resourced with high quality, detailed materials
We think carefully about how we communicated knowledge and information. From 100% sheets that ensure all learners have a clear overview to booklets that support the delivery of our curriculum, we ensure that staff have adequate knowledge and skills to effectively design and enact the curriculum. Evidence-lead training and instructional coaching supports all staff to adapt, scaffold and stretch curriculum resources, where necessary, to ensure that they are meeting the needs of all learners.
Aspirational, inclusive and diverse in content
We want the best for our pupils and have high expectations for all pupils in every year group. These aspirational targets are key to the long term success of our vision. Our curriculum is diverse across all subject areas both within units and across them, thinking carefully about not only the knowledge that pupils learn but how that knowledge base has been constructed. We want to ensure that pupils can see himself represented in our curriculum and have therefore intentionally chosen texts and materials that reflect this. Our curriculum is inclusive and accessible to all pupils, with careful scaffolding, flexible groupings and additional support available when needed.
Rigorously assessed and promotes rapid progress
It is only by carefully assessing our pupils that we can truly know that they are remembering the knowledge and developing the skills that underpin our curriculum. Through low stakes retrieval and quizzing in every lesson, to termly summative assessments, we are constantly checking, re-planning and revisiting concepts to ensure that pupils are committing their knowledge to their long term memory and making rapid progress.
Over the last eight years, our Phase 1 and 2 curriculum has been preparing pupils with the building blocks of all further learning. As pupils move into Phase 3, they will spend their time on a broader range of subjects, with subject specialists, preparing them to make the right choices for their GCSEs and beyond. We want to build on our first set of GCSE results, helping our pupils to achieve even more of the top grades, and supporting them into the very best universities and apprenticeships. As a school, we believe that a solid understanding of English and maths will support all pupils to achieve highly, and so these subjects will continue to form the foundation of our curriculum.
However, we also encourage our pupils to follow their own interests and develop into well-rounded learners so, from Year 6, pupils will have the opportunity to study a wide, academic and rigorous curriculum, and benefit from numerous extra-curricular opportunities to stretch their learning and spark their passions.
Please note that parents and carers have the right to withdraw their child from all or part of RE. Please contact the Co-headteacher if you wish to exercise this right. For more information about our curriculum please contact rafinfo@reachacademy.org.uk
Our subject overviews
We offer a range of subjects to all ages. As an all-through school, we’re able to provide an extensive education that spans many years. Browse our A-Z of subject overviews below:
Courses at Key Stage 4
GCSE English Language

GCSE Religious Studies

A-Level French (via Languages for All)

BTEC Health and Social Care
A-Level Psychology (Social Sciences)
A-Level Sociology (Social Sciences)
The Reach Out Curriculum
We are working with schools across the country to support their curriculum in History and Geography at Key Stage 2 and 3. We are delighted to be working with Pearson to share our Primary History and Geography curriculum, developed at Reach Academy Feltham over the past five years.
More about Reach Academy Feltham

Wraparound care for Primary children
Our pre-school and after-school care
Kid Space @Reach
Busy parents sometimes need the flexibility of a longer day…and children love it too!
Reach School’s wraparound care means that you can relax knowing that your child is in safe hands and having fun until you are ready to collect them.
We provide a breakfast club between the hours of 7.30am and the start of school. Children can have breakfast to fuel their day, play games, draw/colour in, or relax in a quiet area before the day ahead. We believe that good food supports children in learning and going on to enjoy a life of choice and opportunity. Breakfast club is £3 from 7.30am for a full session until the start of your child’s day. The children will go directly to their classroom after breakfast club.
Reach Academy Feltham is part of the national rollout of the government’s ‘free breakfast clubs programme’ which gives children a soft start to the day, helping them feel ready to learn. This means we are able to provide a free breakfast to all children from Reception-Year 6 for 30 minutes prior to the start of the school day. Teaching at RAF
Explore our commitment to excellent teaching and professional development
Excellent outcomes
We know that a great teacher is the single biggest factor in determining excellent pupil outcomes. We invest heavily in thinking about what great teaching and learning looks like and how we support our teachers to get better everyday.
Our guiding principles
At Reach we have 6 guiding principles that we believe facilitate consistent, excellent learning. Each guiding principle is broken down into habits to support teachers in isolating and practising areas of their teaching so they can continue to get better every week throughout their career.
Classroom culture
Use Teach Like a Champion (TLAC)1 strategies and Reach routines to facilitate a productive learning environment.
Planning
Maximise curriculum impact through double planning, scripting and excellent subject knowledge.
Exposition
Use direct instruction to explain new concepts, processes and skills with clarity.
Questioning
Use questioning to increase thinking ratio, maintain motivation and gather information on pupil progress.
Practice
Allocate time for practice using tasks and scaffolds designed to facilitate persistent learning.
Feedback
Support pupils to make effective progress by providing relevant, timely and constructive feedback.
Our aims
Professional Development
At Reach we devote time to instructional coaching of all staff to ensure that everyone is supported and challenged to continuously improve the outcomes of all pupils.
Teacher Training
Our teacher training is community-focused, relationship-driven and classroom-based to rapidly develop the practice of our trainees in both Primary and Secondary schools.

pageCache.pageTitle: Behaviour and Attitudes - Reach Academy Feltham
pageCache.text:
Behaviour and Attitudes
Only with a strong relationship are we able to do the work of character education
We know that powerful relationships are central to the work that we do at Reach Academy Feltham, and therefore we invest in all relationships. An analysis of our exam cohorts since the school opened show a close correlation between levels of progress and the depth of relationship between the school’s staff, pupils and families. These relationships must be based on trust and require tenacity from all parties to maintain over the course of life in an all-through school.
In order to be able to think about behaviour and attitudes we must also think about the education of a pupil’s ‘character’. We need to be clear that the relationships that we have with children, their families and each other, are the living proof of what emotional intelligence and resilience looks like. Only with a strong relationship are we able to do the work of character education.
Through a varied character education programme:
Our method:
A key intention of the character education programme at Reach is to make sure that pupils leave Reach Academy knowing how to behave in society and can become positive role models within it. Outstanding behaviour is not only vital in the wider world but also within school to allow the pupils to be successful and allow others to learn in a positive learning environment. That said, learning such behaviours takes time and it is important to teach pupils how to behave, forming these behaviours as a habit, as opposed to just telling them. The reward and sanction system at Reach Academy is intended to teach pupils how to behave both in school and beyond, working alongside our behaviour policy and form curriculum.
Consistency is key to support pupils in building positive behaviours as a habit. Pupils need to be aware that the same behaviours will result in the same reward or consequence in all of their lessons and that the expectations of their behaviour will be the same at all points of the school day. In order to achieve this Reach operates a shared language across all phases within the school with any adjustments according to age made explicit to pupils during transitions. The foundations of the behaviour system, merits and demerits, are used across all phases in the school so pupils are clear when their behaviour is positive or negative. This, alongside a strong reward system will encourage pupils to continue to demonstrate positive behaviours as routine. A centralized behaviour system also serves to show pupils that they are responsible for their actions equally at all points in the school day and they will be held to account as such.
It is important to use positive reinforcement to teach pupils how to behave alongside the use of sanctions. Pupils need to be aware that their actions can have both positive and negative outcomes and, by using a system of rewards, pupils will continue to demonstrate the positive actions until they become routine. Again, this has been planned throughout the school to use the same language and adapt to the age of the pupils. There is a reward stream for the individual and one for the team to show pupils the importance of working for themselves but also the contribution they can have as part of a wider team or community.
In phases 1 and 2, a team is awarded a marble for the class demonstrating our values collectively. This marble is added to a jar and once full the team is awarded a Reach Prize as a class. The class will be constantly working towards this reward, it is just a matter of how quickly they can achieve it. This develops in phase 3 to the Reach Score in which the team is given a score at the end of each class based on the values and, at the end of term, if the average is over 4.6, the team receives the Reach Prize. The development here is that the team may not receive the Reach Prize and will instead spend time working with their form teacher to reflect on the team performance to improve next term.
Alongside this there is a system of individual reward. Pupils in phase 1 and 2 will often receive immediate praise in the class to also share with their families at home. This is to reinforce the positive behaviours that are expected and constantly refer to them to build positive routines. This can include merits certificates or values certificates. This system develops in phase 3 and 4 to a payslip system in which pupils are given a payslip each week summarising all of their positive and negative behaviours across all lessons and given an overall score. These scores can determine various rewards over a period of time allowing pupils to reflect on their own behaviours and work towards desired goals. Over a week if a score of 75 is met pupils will be able to go to enrichment, over a term they will receive a wristband depending on their average and, over a year, if a score of 100 is achieved they will get to attend the residential trip. This teaches the pupil that they are accountable for their behaviour not just in the short term but over a much longer period and should be demonstrating the positive behaviours expected of them constantly.
As pupils develop they are held to greater account for their behaviours. As an all-through school, we have designed our sanction system to take the age of the pupil into account when they are given consequences for their behaviour. This includes the length of the consequence and how long a consequence remains with the pupil. An example of this is the demerit system. Across all phases, 3 demerits will trigger a sanction however the length of time a pupil has a demerit for changes depending on age alongside the length of the consequence.
We analyse data in a number of ways to direct intervention where required. This can include analysing positive and negative behaviours at a pupil, group, teacher or class level for trends as well as looking at payslip scores to direct intervention such as through coaching. Data is analysed weekly for short term intervention and in greater detail each cycle to create action plans for the forthcoming cycle. This directly informs the pastoral team where to direct intensive coaching to direct intervention to the pupils who are struggling most at that specific time.
As pupils navigate these decisions, a programme of support will also be offered to guide pupils during their development until they are able to independently make decisions that positively impact their future. The benchmarks for this development can be seen below and the implementation of the different aspects of this programme can be seen throughout this document.
Explore Reach Academy Feltham

Enrichment
Find out why enrichment is important to us and our pupils
Why enrichment?
The purpose of enrichment at Reach Academy Feltham is to introduce students to topics and opportunities that they don’t have access to as part of the academic curriculum. Enrichment aims to broaden students’ aspirations and foster a love of learning outside the curriculum. Enrichment is run in phase 2 and phase 3 across the phases, which allows students across years 3-5 and years 6-8 to interact, with older students taking leadership roles.
Enrichment options
Enrichment options in Phase 2 and 3 deepen learning offered in academic subjects or provide access to new disciplines. Examples are Science Club, Coding, Politics Club, Debating, Board Games, Sewing and many more. Sports options are also available to encourage healthy living and varied forms of exercise. Our enrichment program is not formally assessed, but each of the enrichment options builds towards a final project or outcome. For example, in our Art enrichment session, students work on creating their own illustrated story book, which they present to other students in the group at the end. Similarly, in our World Board Games option, students design and create their own board game and present this to other students in the group.
Accountability and reward
As pupils grow older, there is a gradual increase in accountability. For phase 2 pupils, enrichment is a weekly occurrence. However, in Phase 3, enrichment also acts as a reward for academic achievements and positive behaviour. It is only available to those students achieving a score of above 75 on their weekly payslip, which emphasises the need for consistent attendance and provides a time slot each week to catch up on key missed work.
Enrichment Events
We also have a variety of events as part of enrichment. These include the Jack Petchey award, Speak Out Challenge, McClaren Day, and Mock Trial. The Jack Petchey award is allocated to a student every month based on nominations made by teachers and their peers. This award gives the student £300 with which they can fund something of their choice for the school – previous winners have chosen to purchase new sports equipment, or to take their form on a team bonding bowling trip. We also use enrichment sessions to focus on musical theatre and dance for our Year 3, Year 4 and Year 5 pupils, who are given the opportunity to be part of the school performance. Our Y10 students take part in the Speak Out Challenge every year – this is a day off timetable in which students learn how to give a speech confidently, and are given the chance to present something that matters to them. The winning students continue into a local competition, and have the potential to continue to the national rounds.

Excellent GCSE Results for Class of 2026
We have seen an exceptional set of Year 11 results this year, with 94% of pupils achieving a Grade 4+ in both English and Maths. This places us substantially above the national benchmark . We are particularly proud of the progress our pupils have made throughout their secondary school journey.
We have seen particularly strong improvements across Maths, English and Science
Co-headteacher of Reach Academy Feltham, Manjit More said:
“We are incredibly proud of everything our Year 11 pupils have achieved. With 94% securing a grade 4 or above in both English and Maths, these results reflect their determination and hard work, alongside the unwavering support of their teachers. Most importantly, our pupils now have a strong foundation from which to take their next steps and enjoy lives filled with choice and opportunity.”
We have enrolled 40 internal pupils and external pupils from 16 other local secondary schools, so we are confident that on September 7th, we will have our target of 95 pupils joining our Year 12. This year also sees our largest ever applications and waitlist for Feltham College.
The Reach Sixth Form Partnership, Feltham College, is delighted to be welcoming back many internal students to start A Levels and BTECs in September, along with a significant amount of external students from other local schools across Hounslow.
Feltham College received an unprecedented amount of applications this year and received exceptional 2026 A level and BTEC results last week. The college is getting ready for an exciting new academic year ahead.

Safeguarding
We commit to keeping our students and families safe and supported.
Safeguarding is the number one priority of everyone at Reach Academy Feltham. We ensure regular and rigorous training and engage with the most challenging topics because we want to be able to walk alongside all of our families, should they need this level of support.
The Reach Safeguarding Team includes:
Director of Families and Safeguarding
Designated Safeguarding Lead and Mental Health Lead
Deputy Designated Safeguarding Lead
Jerome Balakistan-Barlow
Trust Attendance Champion, Deputy Designated Safeguarding Lead
Family Support practitioner
At Reach Academy Feltham there is a vast range of support available to pupils during their time with us. We strive to ensure all pupils are happy, healthy and safe and achieving their full potential.
A supportive practice is embedded throughout Reach Academy Feltham; we ensure every child is supported and encouraged to be the best they can be at every level; from making sure they are organised for their lessons and the day ahead, or supporting them in making sure they are taking the right options and choices for Year 10. Our pupil support provision also offers a number of interventions for pupils who need additional support:
Safeguarding concerns
At Reach Academy Feltham, we strive to make sure all our students are safe in school, at home, online and in the community. It is every staff member’s responsibility to ensure our students are safe and secure and to promote their personal safety and well-being. If a child makes a disclosure of any form of abuse we have a legal duty to act upon this information. It is standard procedure to inform the local authority of this disclosure and to seek advice and guidance. It is best practice to inform parents and carers of the disclosure, however in some instances we are advised not to by children’s services and they will contact parents/carers directly. We appreciate that this can be a particularly difficult circumstance to deal with and we commit to support families as a unit to ensure everyone is safe and happy.
Please see our safeguarding policy for more detailed information on our procedures.
Legislation
Keeping children Safe in Education
Working together to safeguard children
Useful information
Here are some useful guidance and support around online harm and safety for different age groups from Hounslow Safeguarding Children Partnership
Here is more information about the government’s consultation on social media: Growing up in the online world: a national consultation – GOV.UK
Worried about a child?
If you are concerned about a child at, please email/contact Georgia Strong: Georgia.strong@reachacademy.org.uk or elly.grantham@reachacademy.org.uk or telephone 020 8893 1099 or Hounslow Children’s services – on 020 8583 6600 option 2
If you are contacting us out of hours (before 8am and after 5pm) you can contact:
Hounslow duty team 020 8583 2222 and ask to speak to the duty social worker or the NSPCC helpline for support and advice for free – call on or contact NSPCC online.
In an emergency please call 999 or in a non-emergency call 101.
Relationships matter
We build strong relationships with pupils and their parents. This begins with a home visit, which enables us to have a breadth of information about every child in our school. These relationships, founded on trust, allow for open and honest dialogue and we make it clear with parents that we are a team, working together to have challenging conversations.
Our Place2Be service provides mental health support through one -to-one counselling using tried and tested methods backed by research. A drop-in service is also available.
We use CPOMs to report concerns and track everything so as not to miss anything which may impact every single child being able to enjoy a life of choice and opportunity.
We have employed a Family Support Worker since the school opened in 2012 and have been instrumental in initiating the SHEL programme (School-Home Engagement Leads) across Hounslow. We also designed and lead the CAPP (Community Action Partnership Panel) which brings together cross-school safeguarding teams and police to ensure better joint working and problem-solving.
More about support at Reach Academy Feltham

Wellbeing Hub
Positively supporting young people’s mental health and wellbeing
What is the Wellbeing Hub?
We are very proud to be members of the Wellbeing Hub – a fantastic resource about young people’s wellbeing and mental health. It offers access to expert help and guidance for pupils, parents and staff.
This external provider is led by therapist Alicia Drummond, and supported by a team with expertise in psychotherapy, psychology and neuroscience.
Interactive Online Platform
It is a live and interactive online platform, offering a proactive approach to young people’s wellbeing and mental health, by providing information and practical support. On the Hub you will find more than 2,000 expert-led, evidence-based resources, and regular podcasts on particular subjects that many parents are facing, including anxiety, autism, ADHD, addictive behaviours around smartphones and gaming and much more.
Monthly Q and A
On the first Tuesday of every month there is a focus on a particular area of mental health and wellbeing, with live Q and A sessions with Alicia Drummond and a team of experts. There is truly something on every subject that both children, young people and parents might find challenging.
Wellbeing Hub Courses
There are a number of age specific courses that parents can join to find out how to navigate certain developmental milestones, whether your child is neurotypical or neurodivergent.
Young People’s Stories
If you want to hear from other young people how they dealt with a number of challenges they faced. They write about a range of issues from the teen social scene, to navigating exams to dealing with addiction on the Hub.
Sign Up to the Wellbeing Hub Now!
We urge everyone in the Reach Schools community to sign up. We believe it will help support the wellbeing and mental health of our young people so that we can help them live a life of choice and opportunity.
